draftPackage.centralQuestion: Why did a painter accused of selling a masterpiece to the Nazis need to prove that he had forged it?
draftPackage.thesis: Confessing forgery challenged collaboration suspicion, but authorship needed material evidence and fraud remained criminal.
draftPackage.viewerPayoff: Understand how a gap in attribution made the fakes persuasive and how separating old support from new paint tested the confession.

segments.text: To defend himself, this painter had to prove his masterpiece was a fake.
In 1945, Han van Meegeren was arrested on suspicion of collaboration. A supposed Vermeer had reached Hermann Göring, a leading Nazi, through an art dealer.
His defense was that he had painted it himself. But some experts resisted believing that their celebrated Vermeers were forgeries.
He had exploited a gap in Vermeer’s known early work. Religious paintings filled what experts expected to find. A prominent scholar endorsed one; a museum bought it.
He used old canvases, then heated modern resin-based paint until it hardened. Cracking that surface made new paint look centuries old.
But court-appointed examiners tested the materials. They found evidence of modern synthetic resin, matching materials from his studio.
X-rays revealed another problem: separate crack patterns in the old layers underneath and the newer painting above.
The evidence supported his confession. An old canvas did not make the painting an old master.
The collaboration case fell away. The fraud did not. In 1947, he was convicted of fraud and forgery, and sentenced to one year.
He had not sold a Vermeer. He had sold the belief that it was one.

review.comprehensionReview: Cold viewer learns why supposed cultural-treasure sale raised collaboration suspicion, why false attribution was credible, how old support can conceal newer paint, and why proving forgery still leaves fraud. No specialist connoisseurship or chemistry vocabulary required.
review.rightsReview: Two inspected archival photographs under explicit Nationaal Archief CC0 dedication, original explanatory graphics, existing OFL Manrope, established local Apache2.0Kokoro. No scholarly figures/scans reused in production; inspected research is consultation-only.

careAssessment.rationale: Historical criminal/Nazi context treated without glamorization, invented danger or rehabilitating culprit. Strong primary technical and period legal reporting support bounded wording; no unresolved central conflict or rights exception.
